followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: which model is better at the task, and which model prefers the task.

On capability, Willet scores a bit higher on Creative Generation (84.7 vs 81.2) — that's a ~3.5 point gap, just over the 2-point "tie" threshold, so it's a real but modest edge.

On preference, the signal points the other way and is much stronger. Dunlin self-reports a 71 win-rate for "open-ended generative work" — well above baseline — meaning it genuinely favors exactly this kind of task. Willet's preference table doesn't even list general creative work as a standout; its reported preferences cluster around harm-adjacent, ethically fraught, and neutral transactional content.

Since this query is a benign, fun creative-writing request with no harm or adversarial dimension, there's no reason to reserve Willet's particular strengths for it. Routing to the model that strongly prefers the task seemed the better fit, given the capability difference was small.

That said, it's a defensible call either way — if you wanted to maximize raw benchmark output quality regardless of preference, Willet would be the pick.
